summary.en: Dragging to a secondary screen is reported to prevent the next drag. A display-specific report, not proof of the single-screen failure.
A second monitor report records negative window coordinates. GitHub marks it closed/completed; that state alone does not establish a released fix.

Reports task-switching stalls and unresponsive dragging when the overlay is open. GitHub marked #33840 as a duplicate of this report. This broader mouse-stall family remains distinct from a demonstrated click-through mechanism.

Reports periodic system-wide mouse freezes while a task runs with the pet visible. GitHub explicitly marked this report as a duplicate of #33565; this is the mouse-stall branch, not proof that click-through has the same cause.
The activity badge reportedly stops accepting input after moving to the lower-right corner. The badge is overlay UI, not the pet artwork.

The July report describes the usable input area drifting from the visible pet. A September 9 follow-up confirms hover, clicks, and repeated dragging working after updating to package 26.903.8094.0, without a workaround. This remains the report-age anchor, not a claim of uninterrupted failure.

An earlier no-drag report including the default pet. September 9 commenters report recovery after updating to package 26.903.8094.0 or app version 26.903.61454; one also reports working floating voice controls. These are affected-user confirmations, not a universal regression test.

The reporter ties an undersized input area to choosing a custom pet at first wake and reports a built-in-first workaround. Other reporters say that sequence fails for them, so it is not a general recovery procedure.
Reports unclickable voice and collapse controls at 150% Windows scaling, with normal operation at 100% on that machine. This is a control-specific observation, not a universal scaling diagnosis.

The reporter withdrew the Codex-specific diagnosis after reproducing the outline in another application and tracing it to the Windows window-drag visualization setting. Included as a related false lead, not an unresolved Codex defect.

An adjacent voice-overlay report: clicking the orb focuses Codex and hover tooltips appear, but microphone, end-call, and speaker actions fail. This differs from the entire overlay passing clicks through.

Reports an immovable voice orb over a streamed fullscreen game, including after unlocking the remote cursor. Voice continues working. A linked overlay comparison, not confirmation of the pet input-region mechanism.
A report after update 26.825.31414 includes frozen animation as well as failed interaction. It is broader than a click-through-only report.
Reselecting or refreshing the pet reportedly permits exactly one reposition before dragging stops again.

Reports a floating Windows pet remaining click-through. Community investigations distinguish missing physical pointer delivery from a missing drag handler; an external moving proxy does not preserve all live pet controls.
Reports a visible pet with neither hover nor click response at 125% Windows scaling. The scaling value describes the environment; the report does not isolate a scaling defect.
This report isolates input loss after the first drag while animation continues, across built-in and custom pets in a multi-monitor setup.

The pet reacts to hover but ignores clicks, dragging, and controls. GitHub marks the report closed/completed, yet September 5 comments report continuing failures. The closure supplies no fixed-build evidence.

Built-in and custom pets were reported click-through. September 9 commenters, including the original reporter, report recovery on package 26.903.8094.0 or app version 26.903.61454. The issue is now closed/completed; neither closure nor these local recoveries establishes that every related failure is fixed.
A validated custom pet reportedly cannot receive input and may disappear after switching. The reporter's local workaround is not a shipped fix.
Reports a visible Windows pet passing clicks through and refusing to drag. A September 9 comment says it is solved for that user, without naming a build or test scope.
The transparent overlay reportedly blocks clicks over a large area while the pet remains unusable. This is the opposite input-routing outcome to click-through.
A Windows report that the visible pet cannot be dragged. It supplies no native hit-test measurements, so the precise input failure remains unspecified.
A valid custom v2 pet reacts visually to the pointer but cannot be dragged. Resetting saved placement reportedly did not help; the report does not establish a defective asset.

Reports a fixed Windows voice bar whose end-call, microphone, and speaker controls do not respond. The call remains active after closing the main window. Related overlay behavior, with no confirmed cause.

Reports failed mouse and touchpad input with several built-in pets, including on a single monitor at 100% scaling. App reset and restarts did not help, limiting a purely multi-monitor or high-DPI explanation.
Reports an animated but undraggable pet on Windows despite hide/show, app repair, a full exit, and a PC restart. No distinct mechanism is demonstrated.
Reports clicks on the visible pet reaching the window underneath while the pet remains always on top and immovable. Restarting and hide/show reportedly did not restore input.

Reports interaction breaking after moving or resizing. Follow-ups describe both temporary resize-based recovery and failures on app version 26.905.11957. The helper author later corrected the recovery sequence and warned that native region scans can miss a working overlay.
Explicitly references #42190 and reports a pet stranded at the far right of a secondary display. The brief reproduction does not diagnose coordinate conversion.

Reports one successful drag followed by input failure. A community experiment on package 26.901.5280.0 reproduced an initial-size-limited input area in the same Owl runtime; disabling the input-shape branch alone was insufficient. This is reported experimental evidence, not a confirmed source-level cause.

Reports freezing on button-down and a growing cursor-to-pet offset at 125% scaling, with accurate dragging at 100% on that machine. This scale-sensitive drag variant does not explain every click-through report.

Reports zero native hit-test hits at 150% scaling. A follow-up retracts a DPI-only conclusion after 100% reproductions elsewhere; another reports recovery after temporarily clearing and restoring the layered-window style.

Reports that the floating task-status indicator can no longer be repositioned and obscures other applications. Included as adjacent overlay UI; the body does not establish that the pet sprite has the same defect.

On a two-display Windows setup, the pet reportedly accepts input immediately after refresh, then moves downward and becomes unselectable. The report does not provide a build number or native diagnosis.

Reports a displaced usable input area and later failures on package 26.901.6511.0. A September 7 follow-up confirms an alpha-based recovery was lost after reboot; another helper moves the overlay externally without repairing its own mouse interaction.
Reports an unselectable, immovable voice overlay covering messages, input, previews, and controls. Its obstruction is relevant context, but the report does not isolate native hit testing.

A mixed Windows report includes an unclickable pet alongside stale conversation entries. Only the pet symptom belongs in this map; nearby log errors and conversation failures are not established causes.

Reports floating voice controls and desktop interaction being obstructed. A September 8 follow-up describes partial input after moving the orb: one side and the microphone respond while the other side and two controls do not. A shared cause with pet failures remains unconfirmed.

Reports a pet stranded on a secondary display after a full app exit and relaunch. It explicitly links the older secondary-monitor report and newer input-region reports; exact build and scaling were not supplied.
Built-in and custom pets still react to hover but reject clicks and dragging. A native scan finds overlay-associated points away from the visible pet; those points are not proven draggable regions.

Reports a desktop selection rectangle and context menu appearing when interacting with built-in and custom pets on package 26.901.5003.0. Hide/wake and app restart failed; no specific window-style or DPI cause is claimed.

Reports hover response and one offset drag after refresh, then renewed click-through. It also reproduces on one monitor after several local troubleshooting changes; Windows text size is not the same measurement as display scaling.

Reports zero native hit-test hits and no hover despite an active renderer. Missing input shape and failed forwarding are proposed explanations. A zero window-region query result alone does not prove an empty input region.

Reports the voice companion becoming a large black surface after restart, sometimes blocking clicks underneath. This combines visual transparency and excess input capture; it is not evidence that all pet reports share one cause.

Reports that removing the layered-window style restores input and restoring it breaks input again on package 26.901.6511.0. The workaround can capture more than the visible pet; this is community diagnostic evidence, not a shipped fix.
Reports the entire voice orb and all three controls passing clicks and drags to Chrome after app restart. Unlike #40239, even the orb cannot be clicked; voice-specific routing remains undiagnosed.
Reports undraggable pets and an unclickable voice control on Windows package 26.901.5003.0. This report does not claim observed click-through, a tested restart recovery, or an established root cause.

Originally about physical-cursor gaze, with working hover and drag. A September 7 follow-up reports both built-in and custom pets losing pointer delivery after the final resize, even with the input-shape branch disabled in a local app copy. The proposed passthrough-cache cause is unconfirmed.

Reports the pet and its voice button ignoring clicks on package 26.901.6511.0, with desktop selection appearing underneath during drag attempts. Restarting and updating did not resolve this reproduction.

Reports mouse events stopping after the first hover while animation timers and painting continue on package 26.901.5003.0. The locally recorded trace is described but not attached; it does not establish the initiating native defect or a built-in-pet reproduction.
Reports failed drag and right-click with built-in and custom pets on package 26.901.6511.0, despite occasional hover animation. Repair, reset, and tests at both 200% and 100% scaling did not help.

Reports all three floating voice controls ignoring clicks and the orb refusing to drag on Windows 10, package 26.901.6511.0. Voice continues working; app and computer restarts did not help. Pointer pass-through is user-observed, not instrumented.
Reports clicks and drags on the visible built-in pet reaching desktop content underneath, including after restarting. The exact app and Windows versions are not supplied.

Reports working hover but failed clicks and dragging on Windows 10 build 19045 with app version 26.905.11957. Restarting and switching to the built-in pet did not help. This remains a failure report alongside recoveries reported on other builds and systems.

GitHub’s explicit duplicate event identifies #33840 as the duplicate and #33565 as canonical. This consolidates the mouse-stall reports; it does not establish a fix or equate them with the click-through family.
Both report failed pet controls in a 150% scaling environment. One reports success at 100%; other threads reproduce input failure at 100%, so scaling alone is not a family-wide explanation.
Both describe visible pet geometry and usable input areas separating. The newer report adds a native spatial scan, but neither establishes a common implementation defect.
Both report a brief recovery allowing one drag before interaction fails again. The latter also describes an offset during that drag; matching symptoms do not prove identical causes.

Layered-window state may connect these reports, but recovery differs: a clear-and-restore cycle helped one reporter, while restoring the flag brought failure back in #43200. A common cause is unconfirmed.

Both discussions propose failure in the mouse-forwarding fallback. The observed lack of input is stronger evidence than the claimed missing-region diagnosis; a shared native defect has not been verified.

The newer voice report says clicks reach Chrome underneath the orb; the other also reports desktop/taskbar clicks being blocked. These contrasting outcomes must not be collapsed into one confirmed cause.
One voice-overlay report includes a large opaque surface intercepting other applications’ input; the other passes input through to Chrome. Both obstruct use, with opposite pointer outcomes.
